title: Application of Artificial Intelligence in the Management of Climate Change-Related Health Issues in Africa
abstract: arXiv:2610.35294v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While climate change disproportionately impacts African public health, AI predictive modeling remains heavily constrained. Using a Synthetic Knowledge Synthesis approach and VOSviewer, we conducted a bibliometric analysis of Scopus-indexed literature, comparing Global and African corpora. Network analysis reveals stark divergences: global research emphasizes complex, predictive models for planetary health, whereas African research focuses on localized, reactive solutions for immediate infectious disease triage. Severe structural barriers in Africa, including compute deficits, data silos, and energy instability, hinder advanced AI scaling. Ultimately, international funding must shift from siloed pilot projects toward building foundational digital infrastructure and localized AI frameworks.

translated_title: 人工智能在非洲气候变化相关健康问题管理中的应用
translated_abstract: 尽管气候变化对非洲公共卫生产生了不成比例的严重影响，但AI预测建模在该地区仍受到极大限制。本文采用综合知识合成方法和VOSviewer工具，对Scopus收录的文献进行了文献计量学分析，对比了全球与非洲两个文献语料库。网络分析揭示了显著的差异：全球研究侧重于面向地球健康的复杂预测模型，而非洲研究则聚焦于针对即时传染病分诊的本地化、反应性解决方案。非洲存在严重的结构性障碍，包括算力不足、数据孤岛和能源不稳定，这些因素阻碍了先进AI的规模化应用。最终，国际资助必须从孤立的试点项目转向建设基础数字基础设施和本地化AI框架。
tldr: 该论文通过文献计量学分析揭示了全球与非洲在气候健康AI研究上的显著差异，指出非洲面临算力不足、数据孤岛和能源不稳定等结构性障碍，并呼吁国际资助从孤立试点项目转向建设基础数字基础设施和本地化AI框架。
en_tdlr: This bibliometric analysis reveals stark divergences between global and African AI-climate health research, identifies severe structural barriers in Africa including compute deficits, data silos, and energy instability, and calls for international funding to shift from siloed pilot projects toward foundational digital infrastructure and localized AI frameworks.
